amendments.rule: A supplied English relative clause does not realize the article that governs it. Where the ASV renders an attributive participle as a finite clause — `τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἐνεργουμένην` → *the power that worketh*, `τὸν καλούμενον` → *which is called* — the relativizer and any copula are helpers on the participle under rules 7 and 9, and the second attributive article stays its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 23. The test against rule 32 is whether the article governs an expressed head noun. `τῷ θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι` → *God who created* has one, so the second article realizes nothing and *who* is the participle's helper; a bare `Τῷ δυναμένῳ` → *unto him that is able* has none, so the article is substantival and takes the pronoun itself. That test decides only the cases where a participle follows, because the participle is what carries the relativizer. It decides the **relativizer** alone and never the determiner, the two being separate questions: an article that **precedes** an expressed head noun of its own is that noun's determiner however the modifier standing between them is rendered, so where a participle intervenes the article takes the English *the* with any case preposition riding along under rule 21, and the participle still keeps the relativizer, any supplied copula and its own verb. `τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἀδελφοῖς` → *unto the brethren that dwelt in Judaea* gives *unto the* to the article, *that dwelt* to the participle and a bare *brethren* to the noun, exactly as rule 22's `τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην` → *even the wisdom that hath been hidden* divides a supplied nominal from the participle's own clause. The `unrepresented` article of this branch is the **second** attributive article, whose noun has already taken the determiner standing in front of it; an article with an English determiner of its own to carry is emptied neither by rule 23 nor by this rule. Where the article's modifier carries **no verb of its own** — a **prepositional phrase**, or a bare **adverb** — there is nothing there to carry the relativizer, so the article keeps the supplied relativizer whether or not it governs an expressed head noun, and the copula goes with the preposition or with the adverb: `τὰ στρατεύματα τὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ` → *the armies which are in heaven* gives *which* to the second article and *are in* to `ἐν`, as `τὰ ἄνω` → *the things that are above* gives *the things that* to the article and *are above* to `ἄνω`. An adverb is no different from a prepositional phrase here, rule 53 already giving an adverbial predicate the supplied copula; and where the article is substantival it takes the supplied nominal along with the relativizer under rule 22, headed on the nominal word and never on the determiner or on the relativizer. Which side takes the English *the* is decided by where the article stands, not by the relative clause. An article that **follows** its noun leaves the determiner on the noun, supplying one there when the noun is anarthrous: `καρπὸν δικαιοσύνης τὸν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ` → *the fruits of righteousness which are through Jesus Christ* gives *the fruits* to `καρπόν` and only *which* to `τόν`, as `κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ` → *as touching the righteousness which is in the law* gives *the righteousness* to `δικαιοσύνην`. An article that **precedes** the noun it governs is that noun's own determiner and takes *the* along with the relativizer, headed on *the*, leaving the noun bare: `τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην` → *the righteousness which is from God* gives the discontinuous *the … which* to `τήν` and *righteousness* to `δικαιοσύνην`, as `τὴν καθ' ὑμᾶς πίστιν` → *the faith … which is among you* does. That is rule 22's determiner clause holding where a head noun is expressed: the article carries the English determiner unless its own noun has already stood in front of it. An article left `unrepresented` in front of such a verbless modifier is right only where the ASV supplies no relative clause at all.
amendments.why: Rule 31 gives two clauses that appear to collide on the shape ACT.11.29 carries — article, participle, then the expressed head noun. Its participle branch says the article 'stays its own unrepresented unit', while its position clause says an article preceding its noun is that noun's determiner and takes *the*. A verse pass applying the participle test literally would empty τοῖς and then have nowhere principled to put the *unto the* the ASV wrote. The amendment separates the two questions in the branch where the collision arises and leaves every other clause of the rule untouched: the relativizer still goes to the participle, the second attributive article is still empty, and the verbless-modifier carve-out is unchanged. It contradicts nothing in the corpus — rule 22's τὴν ἀποκεκρυμμένην already divides a supplied determiner-plus-nominal from the participle's clause the same way — and it is stated narrowly enough not to reach a substantival article, which rules 22, 32 and 90 already govern.

conventions: Supplied English lexical content is folded onto the token whose own English it completes rather than marked `added`: *the matter* on ἐξετίθετο at 11:4, *mine eyes* on ἀτενίσας at 11:6, and *he did* on the dative ἡμῖν of the elliptical comparative at 11:17. The chapter therefore carries no `added` unit anywhere, and each fold names the competing rule 5 reading in its own note.

A σύν-compound verb's dative complement takes the English *with* on rule 106's oblique arm — 11:3 συνέφαγες αὐτοῖς → *with them*, 11:12 συνελθεῖν αὐτοῖς → *with them* — while an **expressed** σύν whose sense the ASV's verb absorbs whole is `unrepresented`, as 11:12 ἦλθον σὺν ἐμοί → *accompanied me* is. What decides between them is whether a preposition is expressed for the English to answer to, never the preverb; one verse writes both.

ἕως is classified an improper preposition under rule 95's lexeme test, against a morph tag that neighbours it with the proper prepositions, so its supplied frame *as far as* is headed on *far* under rule 71 at both 11:19 and 11:22.

report: Checked all 45 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the ASV's own wording or by a different Greek configuration, so no patch is owed. The article's five-way T→N bucket is the ordinary the / of the / unrepresented split, decided each time by whether the ASV wrote a determiner (11:9, 11:10, 11:23 write none for heaven, God, purpose, heart); εἰς, ἐπί, δέ and καί vary only in the English word the ASV chose.

Compound-verb handling (rule 106) audited across thirteen verses and is uniform. Where the preverb and an expressed preposition are the same morpheme and the ASV wrote one English word, the preposition takes it and the verb goes bare: 11:8 εἰσῆλθεν/εἰς, 11:11 ἐπέστησαν/ἐπί, 11:12 εἰσήλθομεν/εἰς, 11:15 ἐπέπεσεν/ἐπί. Where they differ or none is expressed, the particle stays inside the verb: 11:2 ἀνέβη 'up' beside εἰς 'to', 11:3 Εἰσῆλθες 'in' beside πρός 'to', and 11:5, 11:19, 11:22, 11:25, 11:26, 11:27, 11:28.

Article handling audited as a block. Second attributive articles before a participle are unrepresented at 11:1, 11:19, 11:21, 11:22 with the relativizer on the participle; 11:13's τόν is unrepresented under rule 32's apposition clause, Σίμωνα having written the antecedent; 11:29's τοῖς is aligned to 'unto the' because it stands in front of its own expressed noun ἀδελφοῖς, which is rule 31's position clause and not a departure. 11:6 τὰ τετράποδα takes determiner plus supplied nominal under rule 102 while 11:30 τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους takes a bare 'the', because 'elders' is a lexical gloss and not a supplied completion — different English, not two analyses. 11:12's τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀνδρός follows rule 57's prenominal-possessor clause exactly.

The candidate table is blind to added units, so I read the dump for the inverse split. The chapter carries no added unit at all: every supplied English word is folded onto the token whose own English it completes (11:4 'the matter', 11:6 'mine eyes', 11:17 'he did', plus the supplied subject and object pronouns throughout). That is one policy applied consistently, and each fold names the competing rule 5 reading in its note. Recorded as a convention.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. σύν at 11:12 is rule 36's absorbed preposition, the ASV writing 'accompanied me' with no word for it; τόν at 11:12 is rule 57's displaced outer article; τόν at 11:13 is rule 32's apposition clause; μέν at 11:19 is rule 70's English-side test, which says in terms that the report is not a correction; τήν at 11:23 is rule 31's closing clause, the ASV supplying no relative clause for the verbless genitive modifier; τῇ at 11:23 is rule 21's determinerless clause, exactly its own τῇ προσευχῇ → 'by prayer'. No accepted edge changed.

Two single-verse judgment calls are already disclosed in their own notes and I left them: 'as it were' on the predicate noun at 11:5, and every man / τις at 11:29. One more I examined and left as accepted: the expletive 'there' at 11:28 sits with μέλλειν rather than with the expressed ἔσεσθαι. Both are defensible and the chapter's other expletives (11:20, 11:27, 11:28 ἀναστάς) are single-verb clauses, so there is nothing for them to be inconsistent with.

11:28's 'in the days of' frame follows rule 67's prepositional-word head (the JHN.12.11 / 2CO.7.4 line) and names the competing EPH/PHP reading in its note, as rule 67 requires. I did not spend the evidence round on which reading neighbouring Acts chapters took: rule 67 leaves the choice open and the note already discloses it, so an answer would not change a defensible edge.
